  The “Wildlife and Safaris” selection featuring Brazil, Chile and Peru
  includes a major 32-day itinerary. Its fauna observations are concentrated
  around Bolivian lagoons and the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador, outside the
  three selected countries. Iguazu, Atacama and the Peruvian Andes add
  landscapes. Shorter nature-oriented journeys are compared below; a forest
  or mountain excursion does not automatically mean dedicated wildlife watching.

## Brazil, Chile and Peru: where animals are seen on the full tour

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The “Wildlife and Safaris” interest applies to the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) featuring Brazil, Chile and Peru. **It is not limited to those three countries:** the route also includes [Argentina](/argentina/), Uruguay, [Bolivia](/bolivia/), Ecuador and Colombia. Observations of flamingos and island wildlife take place in Bolivia and Ecuador. The 15- and 18-day programs considered below have the “Nature” interest but are not tagged “Wildlife and Safaris”: they are alternatives for comparing landscapes, not members of the current wildlife selection.

This distinction matters when traveling for nature: the famous Bolivian lagoons must not be presented as Chilean, nor the Galápagos Islands as part of Peru. It is more useful to picture the whole route as a succession of ecosystems: Atlantic Forest in Brazil, the dry expanse of northern Chile, then Peru's high-altitude and humid mountain regions.

The existing programs also mix activities. They combine natural attractions with city tours, culture and archaeology. A thematic tag does not mean wildlife observation every day or the presence of a biologist guide.

## Brazil: why Iguazu is more than waterfalls

In Brazil, the central nature day of most itineraries is devoted to [Iguazu Falls near Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The national park preserves a section of Atlantic Forest with substantial biological importance; the Brazilian side offers broad views of the cascades, river valley and surrounding vegetation. It is a good place to encounter the subtropical environment after the city days in Rio.

The Iguazu forest is home to many birds, mammals and reptiles. But an ordinary walk on developed viewing paths is not a private photographic safari. Even where rare species live in the region, their presence in the wild does not guarantee sightings on a tourist excursion.

On the 18-day tour under consideration, the Bird Park and Macuco Safari are offered as optional additions. Seeing birds in aviaries and taking a forest road and boat trip toward the waterfalls does not constitute an included excursion specifically searching for wild animals.

[Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) is also surrounded by striking green slopes; Corcovado is part of the natural landscape of [Tijuca](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/). But on mixed itineraries, the Corcovado excursion primarily focuses on views and a city landmark. **The Amazon rainforest and Pantanal are not automatically included in the selected trips** merely because Brazil is one of the countries.

## Chile: Atacama's actual role in the itinerary

The [15-day journey through Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) includes [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [Valparaíso with Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) in Chile. These stages cover cities, Pacific coastal views and historic neighborhoods; the program does not include a separate extended desert expedition.

For northern Chile's desert scenery, consider the [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/). It includes a flight from Santiago to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). A 4WD journey then begins across the Bolivian border. The days around Laguna Verde, Laguna Colorada and Uyuni take place **in Bolivia**, even though they follow Chile's desert section geographically.

Protected areas around San Pedro support flamingos and other species adapted to saline high-altitude waters. A visit to specific lagoons in a Chilean reserve cannot be considered included, however, unless the itinerary lists it. Some routes offer an evening astronomy excursion: seeing the night sky over the desert is a remarkable nature experience but is different from observing animals.

## Peru: Machu Picchu and Titicaca from a nature perspective

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is often regarded solely as an ancient Inca city. In fact, the historic sanctuary lies amid mountain slopes and tropical forest on the eastern side of the Andes. UNESCO recognizes both its cultural and natural importance. On our itineraries, exploring archaeological structures is the principal activity of the day; an independent natural-history hike or wildlife observation in the forest requires separate confirmation.

The [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) is compelling for its terrain, agricultural terraces and changes in elevation. Longer journeys also reach [Lake Titicaca near Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The lake introduces the high-altitude natural environment, while a visit to the Uros Islands explores local life and traditions. It would be misleading to replace a cultural visit with a promise of observing rare wildlife.

**The Galápagos Islands feature only in certain longer programs and are part of Ecuador**, not the Peruvian stage. The [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) does include them, with one of two alternative marine excursions: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. Travelers whose main priority is observing wildlife should compare that additional Ecuadorian section rather than focus only on the three selected countries.

## Which option best represents the nature theme

| Program | What nature offers |
|---|---|
| [4 countries, 15 days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) | Iguazu, Chilean coastal views, Peruvian Andes |
| [5 countries, 18 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) | Iguazu, Atacama and Bolivia's highlands |
| [8 countries, 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | An Ecuadorian section featuring the Galápagos |

The dynamic table below shows the 32-day tour with the “Wildlife and Safaris” interest. In the comparison above, the 15- and 18-day programs are included as nature-focused alternatives. Scenic itineraries without those animal observations can be compared in the [nature travel selection](/multi-country/brazil_chile_peru/interests/nature/). On a multi-country journey, observations can take place beyond the countries named in the selection: check the full route and individual days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The four-country tour is shorter and does not include the demanding Bolivian off-road section. It suits travelers who want Iguazu, cities and Machu Picchu. Five-country options add a different natural experience: high-altitude deserts and salt flats. Here the amount of 4WD travel and the altitude become more important than the number of regular sightseeing excursions.

For observing seabirds and marine animals around islands, the 32-day itinerary is the closer match within the current selection. It is an entirely different choice in duration and budget, covering many more countries. Do not set a future price based on a shorter trip; compare the conditions of each specific program.

## Season and clothing: three climates, no universal packing list

Iguazu lies in the humid subtropics. Atacama is much drier, but a dry climate does not mean warm nights, especially at altitude. Cusco, Machu Picchu and Titicaca differ in elevation and rainfall. A single “South America” temperature is not enough to choose a travel month.

For Iguazu, pack light clothing, rain protection and shoes with reliable soles. For northern Chile and especially the Bolivian highland section, take warm layers and protection from wind and sun. For Machu Picchu, comfortable shoes are useful on wet steps and in changing weather. The final list depends on dates and confirmed excursions.

The most important medical difference on extended routes is **the elevation of overnight stays**. After San Pedro de Atacama, the five-country program continues through Bolivia's highlands. Cusco is also high in the Andes. Medical guidance emphasizes that the pace of ascent, acclimatization and individual sensitivity matter more than overall fitness. Anyone with cardiovascular or respiratory conditions should discuss the itinerary with a doctor before booking.

When planning, we help compare the seasons of the selected natural sites, flight routes and transfer durations. Adding a separate birdwatching outing or removing city stops would be a change to the program requiring agreement.

## Frequently asked questions about nature tours in Brazil, Chile and Peru

### Is the Amazon or Pantanal included in the selected journeys?

On the programs listed, Brazil's nature experiences mainly focus on [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Amazon and Pantanal cannot automatically be counted among the stops of a major tour featuring Brazil. For a different nature focus, explore [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) with specific itineraries.

### Will we see flamingos in Chile?

Flamingos inhabit parts of Atacama, but an included tour may feature only San Pedro de Atacama and the crossing into Bolivia. Birds also live at Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons, though sightings of a particular species are not guaranteed. Check the day's program and optional excursions.

### What makes Machu Picchu interesting to a nature lover?

It is an archaeological complex amid mountains and tropical forest. The historic sanctuary protects both the monuments and their surrounding environment. A standard excursion concentrates on the complex itself; hikes on separate trails and wildlife watching are different activities.

### Can I choose a tour of only the three named countries?

The 32-day tour in the current wildlife selection also includes Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, Ecuador and Colombia. Shorter nature-oriented programs are included here for comparison. A trip limited to Brazil, Chile and Peru can be discussed as a customized redesign of the route.

### Are sightings of rare animals guaranteed on any of these tours?

No. Natural areas, protected parks and marine excursions offer opportunities to see animals, but sightings of particular species depend on season and circumstances. It would be wrong to guarantee them solely on the basis of a thematic label.

## Brazil, Chile, Peru and Uruguay: a journey beyond four countries

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} including these four main countries, but **selecting four countries does not mean the complete tour visits only four**. Travelers start on Brazil's Atlantic coast, then enter Uruguay via Argentina. After returning to Buenos Aires, they fly to Chile; Peru is reached through high-altitude Bolivia.

The [20-day six-country group tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) visits [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), both sides of [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), Buenos Aires and [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). Santiago, Atacama, Uyuni, Lake Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima follow. The [32-day eight-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) begins in São Paulo and continues through Ecuador and Colombia after Peru. Those are additional countries, not twelve days of leisure in the four selected ones.

## What to visit in each country

| Country | Main stops |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Rio, Iguazu |
| Uruguay | Montevideo |
| Chile | Santiago, Atacama |
| Peru | Titicaca, Machu Picchu |

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the program includes Corcovado with the Christ statue and Sugarloaf Mountain. Travelers then see the falls from the Brazilian side and also the Argentine side: this is a separate border crossing that requires documentation. A ferry excursion from [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) returns to Argentina, rather than continuing overland from Uruguay to Chile.

After a flight to Santiago and another to Calama, a completely different stage begins. [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) is the starting point for the mountain section, followed by Bolivia's lagoons, [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and La Paz. In Peru, the journey travels via [Puno and Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) to Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Removing Bolivia would require a substantial redesign.

## Choosing between 20 and 32 days

| Tour | Key difference |
|---|---|
| [6 countries, 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Ends in Lima |
| [8 countries, 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | Continues to Ecuador and Colombia |

Both programs include 4-star hotels, domestic flights, excursions and transfers according to their respective terms. International flights are listed as excluded. The 20-day tour expressly includes ferry tickets for Buenos Aires–Montevideo–Buenos Aires. The 32-day tour offers optional activities at Iguazu and Atacama that cost extra. Compare what is actually included and excluded on each itinerary, along with the total holiday duration.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If the Andes are your main reason for traveling, also compare the [Bolivia, Chile and Peru selection](/multi-country/bolivia_chile_peru/) to decide whether adding Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires and a ferry day in Uruguay is worthwhile.

## Climate: one packing list for the ocean, another for the Altiplano

For walks around Rio and Iguazu, pack lightweight clothes and protection from rain and sunshine. Bolivia's and Peru's high-altitude sections require warm layers, wind protection, comfortable closed shoes and time to adapt physically. The itinerary includes a stop in San Pedro de Atacama before the off-road expedition, but altitude sickness remains a risk. Discuss any medical conditions that could make altitude dangerous with a physician in advance.

Check weather forecasts for individual places and dates: Rio, Iguazu, Santiago, high-altitude lagoons and Cusco differ in temperature, rainfall and elevation. The contrast between a daytime walk and an overnight stay on the Bolivian plateau matters especially. A single average temperature “for Chile” or “for Peru” says little about this journey.

## Documents, payments and connections

For Russian citizens with ordinary international passports, Brazil's consulate confirms visa-free short tourist visits of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Uruguay's Ministry of the Interior also lists Russia among the countries whose citizens do not need a tourist visa. Nevertheless, **requirements for Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru must be checked separately**, taking into account the actual ports of entry, citizenship, transit airports and travel dates. The Iguazu section involves crossing from Brazil into Argentina, and travelers re-enter Argentina after Montevideo.

Budget for Brazilian reais, Uruguayan, Chilean and Argentine pesos, bolivianos and Peruvian soles. Tour prices quoted in US dollars do not mean dollars are convenient for every small local purchase. Before departure, check whether your specific bank card works internationally, the availability of cash, and spending on shopping and meals outside the program.

On this route, do not eliminate the time buffer between a flight, ferry and border control. We help coordinate the stages and passport-specific document checklist, as well as select sensible connections. The entry time for [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) also needs to be fixed separately: Peru's government ticketing system sells admission for a particular route, date and time slot.

## Frequently asked questions about Brazil, Chile, Peru and Uruguay tours

### Can we see both the Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazu?

Yes. Both programs include both sides of the falls. Documentation for entering Argentina is necessary, even if the user selected a filter naming four other countries.

### Does Uruguay take several days?

No. Montevideo is a one-day ferry excursion from Buenos Aires with a return in the itineraries considered here. It introduces the capital rather than touring the entire country.

### Why travel from Chile to Peru via Bolivia?

On both existing itineraries, this section is dedicated to Bolivia's lagoons, [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and La Paz. Going directly from Chile to Peru would mean removing a substantial part of the program.

### What must be confirmed before paying?

The full country count, nationality-specific visa and transit requirements, included flights, the ferry day in Uruguay, the demands of high-altitude travel and the exact Machu Picchu admission slot.

## Where the real adventure lies in these itineraries

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Brazil, Chile, Peru and Uruguay among the main countries and an adventure theme. The options are [six countries in 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [eight countries in 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Both routes also include Argentina and Bolivia; the latter adds Ecuador and Colombia. **The filter heading does not describe a complete route limited to four countries.**

The main difference between stages is the kind of exertion. At [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), travelers follow viewing walkways and viewpoints; in Chile they prepare for high-altitude travel; in Peru they explore the Andes and Machu Picchu. [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) provides a cultural stop and a break between more demanding days.

| Stage | Kind of exertion |
|---|---|
| Iguazu | Walking, humidity |
| Atacama | Altitude, dry air |
| Peru | Andes, steps |
| Montevideo | City sightseeing |

Multi-day independent treks, mountaineering and rafting cannot be inferred from a thematic label alone. Check the days of the specific tour and distinguish included activities from optional excursions.

## Brazil: walks near the waterfalls and an optional boat

The route first introduces [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain. These are city excursions to viewpoints, not sporting ascents. After a flight to Foz do Iguaçu, the nature section begins: a walk on the Brazilian side of the falls, followed by the Argentine side, which is already in another country on the full journey.

Prepare for wet paths, spray and hot, humid weather around the waterfalls. Shoes with dependable grip are more useful here than heavy trekking boots designed for long independent mountain journeys. Some programs offer the [“Macuco Safari” experience](/brazil/foz-do-iguacu/macuco-safari-program-forest-boat/) with a boat near the falls, but **it costs extra** when explicitly described as optional on the selected itinerary. Do not count it as mandatory included activity without checking that option.

Crossing to the Argentine side and the subsequent flight to Buenos Aires leave limited time for spontaneous additions. If you want a full extra day for nature trails, arrange it before booking the domestic flights.

## Chile and Bolivia: why the most demanding stage lies outside the filter

After Argentina and Uruguay, the journey continues to [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), then flies to Calama with a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The Chilean stop is important preparation for the Altiplano route. These journeys offer an optional evening astronomy tour, a separate activity rather than a mandatory adventure stage.

**The main off-road itinerary starts after crossing into Bolivia.** In 4×4 vehicles, travelers pass through the Laguna Verde area, high-altitude geysers, colorful lagoons and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Here adventure means remoteness from towns, long travel on rough tracks, cold and altitude. Border controls and weather mean such a day cannot simply be shortened into a quick outing.

Altitude affects people differently, regardless of how far they can run at home. When selecting the itinerary, consider gradual acclimatization, rest and access to assistance. Anyone with heart or lung conditions or previous altitude problems needs personalized medical advice.

## Peru: visiting Machu Picchu is not trekking the Inca Trail

After Bolivia's La Paz and the Titicaca area comes the Peruvian section. Via [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), travelers continue to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), visit [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and end that part of the program in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).

On these itineraries, Machu Picchu is visited as a **one-day sightseeing excursion**, not a multi-day hike along the Inca Trail. Admission requires a preselected sightseeing circuit and time slot; tickets and connecting transport must be coordinated. The word “adventure” in the catalog does not add a different ascent or broader access to the archaeological site.

Peru combines altitude, steps, long bus journeys and packed city sightseeing. To enjoy the mountains, consider the number of consecutive travel days, overnight locations, free time and your own pace rather than the trip length alone.

## Choosing between 20 and 32 days

The [20-day program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) follows a sequential route through Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Montevideo, Santiago, Atacama, Bolivia and Peru. It suits travelers who want to complete the main stages in less time and are comfortable with a tight schedule.

The [32-day program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues to Ecuador, the Galápagos Islands and Colombia. Additional countries broaden its cultural and natural scope, but **do not automatically make the four-country section more athletic**. The longer option involves more flights, transfers and geographical changes; it makes sense to choose it for the extended itinerary itself.

Before travel, we help coordinate flights, land-border crossings and connection buffers, and clarify how citizenship affects visas and border formalities. Brazil, Chile, Peru and Uruguay have different currencies and payment practices; card reliability and the need for cash should be checked for the specific route and dates rather than extrapolated from one country to all the others.

## Frequently asked questions about adventure itineraries

### Is trekking mandatory on these tours?

The reviewed programs chiefly consist of sightseeing, walks, a high-altitude off-road journey and transfers. Multi-day independent mountain trekking is not listed as part of the base itinerary.

### Why does a journey through four selected countries include Bolivia?

The selection shows tours containing the four chosen main countries; it does not exclude other countries on the route. Bolivia's off-road section is a substantial component of both matching products.

### Which section requires the greatest caution about altitude?

Above all, San Pedro de Atacama, Bolivia's highlands, La Paz and the Titicaca area. The demands come from altitude combined with long road journeys and temperature changes.

### Can we add more active excursions at Iguazu?

Additional options do appear in tour descriptions, but their inclusion and price depend on the selected product. An extra day may require changes to domestic flights and accommodation.

## Four countries and different eras of South American history

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [20-day journey through six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and a [32-day program through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Both include Brazil, Chile, Peru and Uruguay as main countries. Both also visit Argentina and Bolivia, while the longer route continues through Ecuador and Colombia. **The “Culture and History” theme describes the entire program, but these four countries do contain several distinct cultural stages.**

| Country | Cultural focus |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Old and new Rio |
| Uruguay | Historic Montevideo |
| Chile | Central Santiago |
| Peru | The Incas and life on Titicaca |

The value of this journey lies in comparing cities and cultures, rather than simply counting monuments. Rio introduces Portuguese heritage and modern Brazil; Montevideo, Río de la Plata traditions; Santiago, the history of Chile's capital; and Peru, the heritage of the Andes long before European colonization.

## Brazil: Rio as a city of several histories

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the route includes Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and the central neighborhoods. In the old city, travelers see churches, cathedrals and buildings associated with colonial history; from the viewpoints, they see the structure of the modern coastal metropolis. Christ the Redeemer itself dates to the twentieth century, so it should not be described as a colonial landmark.

A more useful theme for Rio is how a port center, a former capital and a modern tourist city developed in the same place. Panoramas and architectural walks complement one another. Unlike a specialist museum tour, the confirmed itinerary has limited time for central-city excursions; additional museums must not be automatically treated as included.

After Rio comes a visit to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and the Argentine side of the falls. This is chiefly a nature-focused stage. Travelers prioritizing culture may view it as a transition between cities, rather than expect a succession of historical museums at each natural attraction.

## Uruguay: Montevideo on one sightseeing day

The visit to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) on these programs is linked to the journey from Buenos Aires and a city tour. The capital's historic area includes old streets, Independence Square, the city cathedral and the port district. The contrast with neighboring Buenos Aires is particularly interesting: the cities share the history of the Río de la Plata region but have distinct national and urban identities.

**One sightseeing day in Montevideo is not a complete cultural journey through all of Uruguay.** On the current itineraries, the visit is primarily an introduction to the capital. Colonial settlements outside the city, wineries and rural estates cannot be promised without a separate route.

The Uruguay section also introduces a specific logistical consideration: the ferry, boarding time, border crossing and onward schedule. When planning cultural stops, account for transport time as well as the hours spent on the tour itself.

## Chile: Santiago's civic history and the onward road to the Andes

In [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a sightseeing excursion covers the central and eastern parts of the city. Its stops include the historic center, Plaza de Armas and the La Moneda Palace area. These offer a view of the capital's civic and administrative life and a point of comparison with Rio and Montevideo.

The journey then heads to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), where the high-altitude crossing toward Bolivia begins. The Chilean desert stage is important to the overall itinerary, but it should not be described as automatically including every archaeological museum in Atacama. The programs offer a separate optional astronomy excursion; its presence does not automatically expand the cultural component.

The move from city to highlands also changes travel conditions: the air becomes drier, nights colder and altitude more apparent. This matters even on a cultural journey because fatigue from the road can affect enjoyment of subsequent excursions.

## Peru: archaeology and the living cultures of the Andes

The most extensive archaeological section lies in Peru. After Bolivia's La Paz and a visit to Tiwanaku, travelers cross the border and head to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). On the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/), they learn about the tradition of constructing floating islands from totora reeds. This is an encounter with living local culture, distinct from a visit to ruins.

The route then leads to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), which preserves monuments from different eras. The sightseeing day includes archaeological sites around the city and Qorikancha. [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is visited on a separate day, with transport arranged in advance and entry along a designated sightseeing circuit. It is not an unstructured walk without tickets: the time and permitted route are agreed beforehand.

The Peruvian stage therefore enables travelers to explore the traditions of Titicaca's inhabitants, the urban heritage of Cusco and Inca architecture in sequence. It is worth giving each story attention instead of reducing them all to “antiquities.” [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) adds another chapter of Peru's history.

## Choosing an itinerary without losing cultural experiences

The [20-day option](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) includes the main cultural stops in the four selected countries, plus Argentina and Bolivia. Its purpose is to cover varied geography in a relatively limited time. The [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) adds broader context: after Peru, the route continues into Ecuador and Colombia with more cities and excursions. This expands the cultural journey beyond the four countries rather than fundamentally changing the landmarks visited in Rio, Montevideo or Santiago.

Compare the order of days: a city tour after a flight feels different from a walk after a restful evening. For cultural sites, advance admission reservations, visiting times and the guide's language for a particular excursion are important. A Russian-speaking guide on one stage does not automatically imply the same language throughout.

We help coordinate transfers and the excursion sequence and, before booking, review travelers' citizenship, country-specific documents and connection conditions. For this combination, border formalities in Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru are as important to planning as individual museum tickets.

To compare tours without a thematic filter, see the [general Brazil, Chile, Peru and Uruguay selection](/multi-country/brazil_chile_peru_uruguay/); for other cultural routes, explore [“Culture and History” journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about cultural itineraries

### Can we visit Machu Picchu on both programs?

Yes. Both the 20-day and 32-day itineraries include [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) as an excursion day. The actual sightseeing circuit and ticket conditions are determined for each departure.

### Are historic sites visited in Uruguay?

Yes, the itinerary includes sightseeing in Montevideo. It does not, however, promise a separate journey through the historic towns and regions of the whole country.

### Are all excursions conducted by Russian-speaking guides?

There is no basis for assuming this applies to every day. The itinerary materials specify different guiding languages. Check the language against the conditions of each excursion on the selected tour.

### Why does a cultural itinerary filtered for four countries enter Bolivia?

Because the four-country list filters their presence within a longer route. The Bolivian stage includes the highlands and [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and forms part of both matching programs.

## Does a trip through four countries include a genuine wine itinerary?

Our selection features the four main countries of the [“Six Latin American Countries in 20 Days: From Rio to Machu Picchu” tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). The complete itinerary visits **six countries**: in addition to Brazil, Chile, Peru and Uruguay, the group travels through Argentina and Bolivia. The filter does not indicate a ready-made, shortened journey through only four countries.

This intersection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}.

There is one principal culinary activity on this journey: **a Maipo Valley winery excursion with a tasting, available at additional cost**. The Santiago sightseeing tour itself is included, while the wine excursion is optional. The program does not list any separately guaranteed, included local-cooking workshops or tastings in the other three selected countries.

This distinction is important. The trip suits travelers who want a broad overview of South America with one wine experience in Chile. A journey where tastings and culinary activities occupy most days would require a different program.

## Chile: how the Maipo Valley option works

The Chilean section includes [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and an opportunity to visit the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/). This wine region lies near the capital and is particularly known for red wines made from Cabernet Sauvignon. Wine itineraries here may include an introduction to an estate and a tasting.

Our offer lists the [Maipo Valley wine excursion](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/) as **an optional addition**: $230 per person with at least 2 participants. It therefore cannot be counted as a service automatically included for every purchaser of the six-country tour. The winery, departure time and possibility of combining the visit with the main city excursion are agreed before booking.

Allow a substantial block of time for a tasting, including the drive from Santiago and back. The itinerary continues the very next day with a flight to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The wine excursion cannot be moved without checking the flight schedule and road logistics. If the tasting is essential, arrange it in advance rather than relying on spare hours after arrival.

The [Chile food and wine tour catalog](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/) offers other options where visiting wineries is an important selection criterion.

## Brazil, Peru and Uruguay: food as part of travel, but not a scheduled excursion

In Brazil, the itinerary visits [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The days are devoted to the city, Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and the falls. Travelers can sample Brazilian food during ordinary meals, but **no separate culinary workshop or winery visit is listed in the program**. Hotel breakfasts do not automatically turn a city tour into a culinary product.

In Peru, the journey takes in [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). Breakfasts and meals according to individual excursion terms are included on these days, but the main experiences involve Andean history, archaeology and transfers. **No separate Peruvian cuisine tastings, guided food market visits or cooking lessons appear in the confirmed itinerary.** Adding such an activity would need to be agreed as a change to the itinerary and budget.

The Uruguayan stage is a ferry trip from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), with city sightseeing and an evening return. Travelers see the port, Independence Square, the center and the old town. A Uruguayan winery or tasting **is not included that day**. Adding a winery outside the city would affect the actual ferry and tour schedule; it is not simply a matter of substituting one urban sight for another.

The complete journey also includes Argentina and Bolivia. Their food cultures can enrich personal experiences, but belonging to a six-country tour does not in itself establish that separate culinary activities are included there.

## Choosing between an overview tour and a true culinary journey

| Goal | What the itinerary offers |
|---|---|
| Wine tasting | Maipo Valley, additional fee |
| Overview of the four countries | Sections of the six-country tour |
| Cooking workshops | Not listed |
| Winery in Uruguay | Not included |
| Archaeology in Peru | Included sightseeing days |

When comparing options, count the **time actually allocated to culinary experiences**, not the number of countries or the names of national cuisines. Most days on this itinerary are taken up by flights, visits to natural attractions and historic landmarks. Wine is an interesting addition, but not the organizing principle of all 20 days.

A separate experience can be built around Maipo, with time for the tasting, suitable transport and rest afterwards. A deeper introduction to Peruvian cooking would require separate culinary stops in Lima or Cusco, which are absent from the original tour. Ada Tours can discuss such changes and match them to the already scheduled transfers, but the specific services, their prices and the feasibility of changes must be confirmed separately.

## Money, borders and baggage: what to consider with the wine option

The six-country route includes several domestic flights, overland transfers and a ferry between Argentina and Uruguay. Preparing documents for only the four names in the catalog would be a mistake. **Citizenship, every actual border crossing and any re-entry** all matter for visa and transit requirements.

Each country has its own currency and payment rules. Discuss the available ways to pay for the optional excursion and personal expenses before departure, especially if the traveler uses Russian-issued cards. It cannot be promised that a particular bank card, US dollar cash or a single currency-exchange method will work equally well in Brazil, Chile, Peru, Uruguay, Argentina and Bolivia.

If you plan to buy wine bottles at a winery, check the customs allowances **at every border you will cross**, the rules for transporting liquids and airline baggage restrictions. Buying wine in Chile partway through a long itinerary is different from making a purchase immediately before a direct flight home: several more countries and flights remain ahead. It is more practical to discuss transportation before the tasting and avoid assuming unconfirmed allowances.

Finally, the Chilean stage precedes the high-altitude regions of Atacama and Bolivia. Health, adequate rest and a measured pace matter, especially when heading into the highlands. A wine day should not take away the time needed for mandatory transfers and acclimatization.

Before the journey, when coordinating the other excursions and the flight from Santiago to Calama. This allows confirmation of timing, availability and the services included in the fee.
